header.running_head: The Story of The Ansaar During the Battle of Hunayn and the Statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ about them

blocks.text: Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Ansaar, "You are like under clothing to me while others are like outer garments. Does it not please you to know that while other people return home with goats and camels, you should return home with the Rasool of Allaah ﷺ?" "Most certainly!" they replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then added, "The Ansaar are like an abdomen to me and a place where special clothing is kept (they are very close to me). If everyone walks a valley and the Ansaar walk another valley, I shall walk the valley of the Ansaar and had it not been for (the great virtue of) Hijrah, I would have been a man from the Ansaar." [^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when some wealth came to Rasulullaah ﷺ from Bahrain whilst the Muhaajireen and Ansaar heard about it from each other, they came to Rasulullaah ﷺ early in the morning. The rest of the Hadith is lengthy, but in it Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned to the Ansaar, "As far as I know, you people turn out in large numbers when situations are hazardous and turn out in small numbers when the occasion arrives for receiving something (you are always there to assist others and care little about receiving things for yourselves)." [^3]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA), "Convey my Salaam to your people (the Ansaar) and inform them that as far as I know, they are extremely chaste and patient people." [^4] Another narration from Hadhrat Anas (RA) states that when Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) visited Rasulullaah ﷺ during the illness in which Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Convey my Salaam to your people (the Ansaar) for they are extremely chaste and patient people." [^5]
The Statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) Passed Away

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Shaddaad (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ visited Hadhrat Sa'd bin Mu'aadh (RA) as he was on his deathbed. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O chief of his people! May Allaah reward you well. You have fulfilled the pledge you made to Allaah and Allaah shall certainly fulfil His pledge to you." [^6]
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No harm can come to a woman whether she stays between two homes of the Ansaar or between her own parents." [^7]
Ahmad, as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.4 Pg.356)
Askari, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.136).
Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.10 Pg.41) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.136). Haakim (Vol.4 Pg.79) has also reported the narration from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi.
